current.text: He was traded to Memphis, where he is the backup center behind Zach Edey.
He wants a bigger role and more three-point attempts.
He can start when Zach Edey misses time. He would have fantasy value as a starter and could be a great late pick if Edey is out longer.
He sprained his ankle two minutes into a preseason game and is not healthy now. The severity is unknown. Yahoo lists him as out (ankle).

The experts disagree on drafting him. One calls him a late stash as insurance for Edey and finds his rankings fair on Yahoo (174) and aggressive on ESPN (146). A newer note questions drafting him at all while he is hurt.
Memphis has a crowded frontcourt and expects an 11 or 12 man rotation. Coach Tuomas Iisalo uses short stints and keeps minutes down, which limits a backup's minutes.
Memphis has a maxed 4-4-4 schedule in our playoff weeks and only 13 back-to-backs, possibly the fewest in the league.

durable.text: He is a good rim protector and a solid rebounder who has added some three-point shooting.
Blocks are his standout category, far above the top 250 pool.
Steals are a clear weakness, among the lowest for his position.
He has not finished a season healthy in the last three or four years and had many ankle injuries last season.

note: Both sites value him at 0 USD, and his ranks (Yahoo 194, ESPN 147) are outside our 144 drafted players. He is mainly a blocks source with a good FG% (about 1.6 BLK on 54% shooting projected) and fits punt STL builds, but as Edey's backup he only matters when Edey is out. Skip him in the auction or take him only as a 1 USD last pick. Early in the season, check his ankle and Edey's health, and pick him up off waivers if Edey misses time.
